subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should automatic sensitive-value sanitization be a core output-delivery security feature, an optional plugin/ClawHub feature using outbound hooks, or remain outside the existing log/tool/transcript redaction boundary?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix defines a new security boundary and user-visible output policy with false-positive, missed-surface, config, and compatibility tradeoffs that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Approve a narrow core security design
options.body: Define a scoped core sanitizer policy with explicit defaults, config/schema/docs/tests, reporting behavior, and reuse of the existing redaction engine before implementation.

options.title: Route to plugin/ClawHub first
options.body: Ask for an installable sanitizer plugin that uses reply_payload_sending/message_sending or other existing hooks, and only open a core API issue if a concrete missing seam appears.

options.title: Limit core to current redaction surfaces
options.body: Declare logs, transcripts, tool/UI payloads, diagnostics, and internal-scaffolding cleanup as the supported core boundary and close or narrow this request accordingly.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core security design
recommendation.body: Define a scoped core sanitizer policy with explicit defaults, config/schema/docs/tests, reporting behavior, and reuse of the existing redaction engine before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: CODEOWNERS explicitly routes security-sensitive code, config, secrets, and docs to this owner group, and the requested feature defines a sensitive-output security boundary.
